trigger: A frozen fusion challenge failed exact L1 routing-distribution thresholds while top-view decisions, fused semantic conclusions, source anchors, disagreement geometry, and missing-view safety remained strong.
lesson: Internal latent routing proportions are not ground-truth probabilities merely because a training author wrote soft percentages. Evaluation should constrain only outcome-relevant routing properties unless probabilities are independently calibrated.
general_rule: For latent mixtures/routers, prefer allowed sets, dominance margins, min/max mass, set-mass bounds, and impossibility constraints over arbitrary exact target percentages.

trigger: Post-result audit discovered that the frozen validator itself was over-specific.
lesson: Do not retroactively change thresholds or reclassify the historical result. Retire the old validator, keep its result immutable, make no model update, freeze a new independent corrected validator, and evaluate the same unchanged checkpoint.
general_rule: Validator correction must be versioned separately from model correction so evaluation mistakes cannot be hidden as model improvements.

trigger: Historical fusion training used exact soft-distribution cross entropy for routing.
lesson: Exact soft-distribution loss is acceptable only as an explicit heuristic, not calibrated truth. Future repair should use differentiable constraint/set-valued routing losses when multiple internal allocations are behaviorally equivalent.
general_rule: Do not train models to reproduce arbitrary evaluator internals when the task admits an equivalence class of correct representations.
